sentences.text: Net interest income compounded at 4.0% a year from FY2016 to FY2025, reaching $16.6 billion [F115][F10], while noninterest income grew at 2.8% to $11.9 billion [F116][F20].

The window is not a smooth compounder: net income fell 28.3% in FY2020, jumped 60.6% in FY2021, then fell 26.8% in FY2022 and 6.8% in FY2023 before recovering 16.0% in FY2024 and 20.2% in FY2025 [D99][D125][D151][D177][D202][D227].
The FY2021 rebound came from a lower credit-loss provision, which fell to a $1.2 billion release as the economy and credit performance improved [X141][P57].

FY2023's expense step-up reflected merger and integration charges and operating costs from the MUB acquisition plus a $734 million FDIC special assessment [P30], lifting the efficiency ratio to its 67.4% window high [D276].
Consumer and Business Banking was the largest segment at 31.0% of FY2025 revenue but shrank 3.9%, subtracting 1.3pp from growth [D251][D252][D253].
That decline came from deposit mix changes and second-quarter loan sales, which cut segment net interest income 4.9% [P6].
Payment Services grew 5.4% and contributed 1.4pp, with its 25.8% revenue share now close to Consumer and Business Banking's [D260][D261][D259].
Payment Services net revenue rose on higher average loan balances, higher loan fees, lower funding costs and higher merchant processing and card revenue from sales volume [P4].
Diluted EPS grew 21.9% in FY2025 against 20.2% net income growth, as the diluted share count slipped 0.2% [D229][D227][D237].
The efficiency ratio was 59.0% in FY2025, just above the 59.3% window median and well below the 67.4% FY2023 high [D220][D277][D276].
At the 14th percentile against seven bank peers, the ratio sits far below the 61.7% peer median [D280][D281].
Noninterest expense fell 2.0% in FY2025 on prior-year merger and integration charges, lower compensation from operational efficiencies and the absence of the FDIC special assessment [D238][P10].
The credit-loss provision was 7.7% of revenue, above the 6.1% peer median and at the 50th percentile of four peers [D221][D285][D284].
Net margin of 26.5% exceeded the 20.2% effective tax rate's drag, with pre-tax income of $9.5 billion against $7.6 billion net income [D223][D215][X55][F30].
Operating cash flow of $8.0 billion was 1.05x net income in FY2025, down from 1.80x in FY2024 and far below the 3.63x FY2022 peak [F60][D216][D191][D140].
Operating cash flow fell 29.8% in FY2025 while net income rose 20.2% [D230][D227].
For a bank, operating cash flow is not a meaningful earnings-quality measure; capital return against net income is the better test [D216].
Buybacks plus dividends of $3.7 billion equaled 48.3% of FY2025 net income, up from $3.3 billion in FY2024 [D218][F30][D193].
Return on average equity was 12.2% in FY2025, above the 11.8% peer median and at the 71st percentile of seven banks [D226][D283][D282].
Loans were 73.5% of deposits, up from 71.8% in FY2024, while the allowance held at 2.0% of loans [D224][D199][D225].
Shareholders' equity rose 11.3% to $65.2 billion in FY2025 [D233][F114].
Buybacks of $489 million and dividends of $3.2 billion were funded from operations, and the diluted share count fell 0.2% [X85][X95][D237].
Long-term debt is not reported after FY2022, when it stood at $39.8 billion [R2][X172].
This is a data gap rather than a credit event, but it blocks any leverage comparison across the last three years [R2].
Revenue fell 2.4% in FY2024 to $27.3 billion, driven by a 6.4% drop in net interest income from higher rates on deposit mix and pricing [R1][D214][D194][P21].
The decline proved temporary, with revenue up 4.4% in FY2025, so the flag is low persistence [D239].
If the efficiency ratio moves back above the 59.3% window median, the FY2025 cost improvement would be reversing [D277][D220].
A credit-loss provision above the 7.7% of revenue reported in FY2025 would signal credit deterioration [D221].
Net interest income growth below the 2.2% of FY2025 would confirm the deposit-mix pressure cited in the FY2025 10-K [D234][P15].
